name: Composite trapezoidal quadrature
definition: For x_i=a+ih and h=(b−a)/n, Q=h[(f(a)+f(b))/2+Σ_(i=1)^(n−1) f(x_i)].
variables: n positive panel count, Q approximation to ∫_a^b f(x)dx
assumptions: Equal spacing and finite endpoint values; second-order error for C² integrands
limitations: An integrable endpoint singularity can make the rule undefined
failure_conditions: An integrable endpoint singularity can make the rule undefined

source.citation: NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions, §3.5(i). https://dlmf.nist.gov/3.5.i

name: Composite Simpson quadrature
definition: For positive even n and h=(b−a)/n, Q=(h/3)[f(a)+f(b)+4Σ_(i odd) f(a+ih)+2Σ_(i even, 0<i<n) f(a+ih)].
variables: Odd and even indices are interior grid points, Q estimates ∫_a^b f
assumptions: Equal spacing and C⁴ integrand for fourth-order error
limitations: Reduced smoothness can remove fourth-order convergence
failure_conditions: Reduced smoothness can remove fourth-order convergence

name: Romberg integration
variables: T(n) composite trapezoidal value on n panels, k grid refinement, j extrapolation level
assumptions: Trapezoidal error has an even-power expansion to the extrapolated order
limitations: Endpoint singularities can invalidate the error expansion
failure_conditions: Endpoint singularities can invalidate the error expansion
computation: 2^k+1 distinct function evaluations with grid reuse and O(k²) extrapolation arithmetic

name: Gaussian quadrature
definition: For a positive measure with finite moments through degree 2n, choose n nodes at the roots of its degree-n orthogonal polynomial and weights w_i=∫ℓ_i(x)dμ(x), where ℓ_i are their Lagrange cardinal polynomials. Q=Σ_i w_i f(x_i) is exact for deg f≤2n−1.
variables: μ integration measure, x_i nodes, ℓ_i interpolation basis, n order
assumptions: Measure has at least n+1 support points; the model specifies the weight before quadrature
limitations: Localized peaks between the nodes can be poorly resolved
failure_conditions: Localized peaks between the nodes can be poorly resolved
computation: n integrand evaluations after constructing the nodes and weights

name: Golub–Welsch quadrature construction
definition: For orthonormal polynomials p_j under μ, set J_ij=∫xp_i(x)p_j(x)dμ(x), 0≤i,j<n. For each normalized eigenpair Jv_k=x_kv_k, set w_k=μ(ℝ)(v_k)_0².
variables: J symmetric tridiagonal Jacobi matrix, x_k Gaussian nodes, w_k weights
assumptions: Known recurrence coefficients and positive measure with at least n+1 support points and finite moments through degree 2n
limitations: Inaccurate recurrence coefficients perturb both nodes and weights
failure_conditions: Inaccurate recurrence coefficients perturb both nodes and weights
